name: The Harvest Below: Ward Nine and the Outer Stack Trials
description: Assembled over four years from stolen HelixCorp internal footage, intercepted medical telemetry, and testimonials recorded in shielded basement locations across the Shelf, this underground documentary details the systematic use of unregistered Tier 1 residents as test subjects for unlicensed chrome augmentation trials and forced BCI substrate migration between 2198 and 2206. Its primary compiler, a former HelixCorp data hygienist known only by the handle Saltmarrow, was found dead in the Lachine overflow channels eight months after the first copies began circulating on physical media — officially ruled an accidental drowning. The film exists in at least three incomplete versions because no single courier ever possessed the full cut; it was deliberately fragmented for distribution safety.
cultural_impact: The phrase 'Ward Nine' entered Shelf vernacular as shorthand for any situation where someone is being experimented on without their knowledge, and the fragmented distribution method — splitting sensitive material across multiple physical carriers — became a standard underground tradecraft protocol referred to as 'Saltmarrow splitting.'
story_hooks: A player character receives one fragment of the documentary embedded in what they thought was a pirated entertainment feed — now they know something dangerous, and someone knows they received it.

A surviving Ward Nine test subject recognizes their own medical telemetry in the documentary fragment circulating in their district and wants to find the rest of the film — or destroy it before HelixCorp traces it back to them.

The three fragmentary versions of the documentary contain a discrepancy: one names a HelixCorp executive still in active senior leadership, while the other two versions have that segment cleanly excised — suggesting the 'authentic' copies have been tampered with after the fact.
